ledger.note: 1226: Lübeck becomes a Free Imperial City. 'In 1226, Emperor Frederick II declared the city of Lübeck to be a Free Imperial City.' The page gives no Barbarossa reference of 1188 and is silent on Danish rule of 1201-1225 and on the 1143 and 1159 foundations (the Hanseatic League page has Henry the Lion rebuilding Lübeck in 1159 after taking the area from Adolf II).

ledger.note: 1806: the Holy Roman Empire dissolves. 'Lübeck became a sovereign state when the Holy Roman Empire dissolved in 1806.' The state itself continues (Free City of Lübeck, 1806-1937; the 711-year-long statehood ended on 1 April 1937), so the end here is the end of the imperial status, not of the state; a French occupation followed on 6 November 1806 and annexation 1811-1813.

wars.name: Danish-Hanseatic War

zones.text: the city of Lübeck (the gazetteer point for Lübeck; the pages name no outlying land before 1359)

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Stralsund (1370) forced Valdemar IV of Denmark and Haakon VI of Norway to grant tax exemptions and influence over the Øresund fortresses for 15 years; 'The treaty marked the height of Hanseatic influence.' The Confederation of Cologne (1368 on the page) was part of it.
wars.note: The page dates the war 1361-1370; it gives no land change for Lübeck.

notes: The Free City of Lübeck page covers the whole statehood 1226-1937; this dossier takes 1226-1806 and the Cliopatria row Free City of Lübeck (1806-1870, group eu-20) continues it, so the successor line is a continuation of the same state (one colour for life). The Hanseatic League is an association that 'lacked a permanent administrative body, a treasury, and a standing military force' and 'never formally founded' (page); it has no territory and is not drawn (no dossier). Lübeck's Hanseatic leadership: 'Queen of the Hanseatic League' in the 14th century, hegemony peaking in the 15th (Hanseatic page). The pages are silent on Travemünde and Ratzeburg, so those are not drawn. Hamburg shares the Bergedorf condominium and needs its own dossier (free imperial city, no Cliopatria row before 1814). Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): counterparts of the Mölln (1359) and Bergedorf (1370, 1420) events set to duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg (the page: Albert V, Duke of Saxe-Bergedorf-Mölln; Eric III; Eric V; that dossier files the 1420 loss); 1420 dated August (Peace of Perleberg, 23 August 1420); Count's Feud belligerent denmark-norway.
